stories.headline: Jeremiyah Love's Ankle Went High, and Tyler Allgeier Just Became the Cheapest Gold in Arizona
stories.read: Schefter put it on the wire Sunday, pardner: the No. 3 overall pick is nursin' a high ankle sprain and he ain't ridin' again this preseason. Arizona says they're hopeful for the September 13th opener against the Chargers, but a high sprain is the kind of busted wing that lingers a month past when the doc says you're fine. Now look at that backfield: James Conner still ain't taken a full snap since last year's foot, Trey Benson's got a bad knee, and the only healthy horse in the barn is Tyler Allgeier. Love's still worth a claim if the saloon discounts him, but you go stake Allgeier right now, because that fella might carry the mail for three weeks while your leaguemates are still readin' yesterday's paper.

stories.headline: Houston Rides to New England and Comes Back With Boutte, and Nico Collins Just Got a Whole Lot Fatter
stories.read: The Texans shipped safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh to the Patriots for Kayshon Boutte on Monday, patchin' a hole blown open when Jayden Higgins tore up his knee in joint practice last week. Boutte put up 551 yards and six scores in ten starts last season, so he's a real receiver, but he's walkin' into a new camp two weeks before the whistle and he don't know the trails yet. The read here ain't Boutte, it's Nico Collins, who was already the belle of that offense and now owns an even bigger cut of the throws with Higgins laid up for the year. Pay whatever the saloon's askin' for Collins, throw a late dart at Boutte in deep outfits, and quit chasin' Higgins entirely.

stories.headline: Woody Marks Is Takin' Half the Houston Backfield, and David Montgomery Drafters Are About to Feel It
stories.read: The Houston Chronicle's beat man says the split between David Montgomery and Woody Marks might not be a clean fifty-fifty, but it'll be close, and camp has looked exactly that way all month. Marks ripped off 37 yards and a score on four totes against the Raiders while Montgomery didn't even dress. Montgomery still gets the money patch work near paydirt, so he ain't worthless, but you're payin' a starter's price for a fella splittin' the reins with a second-year pass-catcher who never leaves the field on third down. Let somebody else pay retail for Monty. Marks is the cheap gold here, and in a league that counts catches he's a flat-out steal three rounds later.
